name: BPJS Ketenagakerjaan — Jaminan Pensiun (pension)

references.title: PP 45/2015
references.quote: JP is 3% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 2% from the employer, charged on wage up to an annually adjusted ceiling (art.28–29). Contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base; a reimbursement is not. Each contribution month is priced on its own wage ("pada bulan yang bersangkutan", art.29(1)), so a deferred earlier month paid as back pay is capped at the ceiling on its own beside this month's wage. Pension age is 56, 57 from 1 January 2019 and one year more every three years — 59 from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2027 (art.15(1)–(3)); a participant still employed may choose to take the pension when work stops, at most three years after pension age (art.15(4)); contributions stop at 59 unless that choice is recorded (to 62). Registration of every worker is mandatory within 30 days of starting work (art.4(1)–(2)); art.5(5) obliges the negligent employer to collect and pay both the worker's and its own contributions besides the art.5(4) sanction; art.3(1) dates the start of benefit protection and art.6 adds the employer's own liability for the benefit meanwhile — neither removes the contribution. JP covers Indonesian nationals only; a foreign national cannot be registered for JP (BPJS Ketenagakerjaan). Existing PP45/2015 art.15(4) and Permenaker29/2015 art.3 allow a confirmed still-employed participant to defer benefits and continue contributions for at most three years beyond pension age; this election is supported in every 2025–2026 seed version. A THR (Permenaker 6/2016 art.2–3) and a bonus are neither upah pokok nor tunjangan tetap, so they are outside the JP wage; the row reads the ordinary pay this run actually pays, not a contract rate.

name: BPJS Kesehatan (health insurance)

references.title: Perpres 82/2018
references.locator: art.30 as amended, art.1 angka 2, art.2, art.5(3)–(4), art.13(1), art.13(5), art.14(1), art.32, art.36
references.quote: Kesehatan is 5% of the monthly wage, 1% from the employee and 4% from the employer, charged on wage between a floor and a ceiling (art.30; art.31 was deleted by Perpres 64/2020 and art.30(2) is the direct-payment rule). Contribution wage is upah pokok plus tunjangan tetap — the standing car, housing and special allowances are in the base; a reimbursement is not. A further family member (a fourth child, a parent, a parent-in-law) is enrolled at the worker's election and costs 1% of the (capped) wage each, paid by the worker (art.5(3)–(4), art.30(1)(b), art.36); the regulation states no ceiling on their number. A participant is every person, a foreigner included, who works at least six months in Indonesia (art.1 angka 2; the same six-month reading JHT, JKK and JKM apply, PP 44/2015 art.1 angka 4); a foreigner on a contract shorter than six months is outside Kesehatan (art.2). Art.13(1) obliges the employer to register itself and its workers "dengan membayar Iuran", art.13(5) leaves the health benefit on an employer that has not registered and paid, and art.14(1) requires each spouse's employer to register and pay. Owner rule 2026-09-30 (arts.30(1), 32(1)–(2) price "Gaji atau Upah per bulan" with the UMK/UMP as its lowest bound and are silent on a part month): the base is the wage paid for the month — basic plus fixed allowances less unpaid days, the same month's-wage reading as JP (PP 45/2015 art.29(1)) — and a month's wage paid below the floor is lifted to the whole floor, not a prorated one; e.g. a joiner on 16 February 2026 at 12,000,000, paid 5,571,428.57 under the DKI UMP 5,729,876: 57,299 / 229,195. Contributions are monthly (art.30, art.32(1) "per bulan"), so a deferred earlier month paid as back pay is floored and capped at 12,000,000 on its own beside this month's wage. A THR (Permenaker 6/2016 art.2–3) and a bonus are outside the base: the row reads the ordinary pay the run actually pays, and the gaji pokok plus tunjangan tetap composition it applies is the one art.33 states for state officials, read for a private-sector worker. Perpres 82/2018 itself fixes the rate and, in art.32, the floor and ceiling; a THR is a separate annual payment, not a monthly component, so it stays outside.

name: Pajak Penghasilan Pasal 21 (income tax withholding)

references.title: PP 58/2023
references.quote: Monthly TER withholding for permanent employees: category A = PTKP TK/0, TK/1, K/0; B = TK/2, TK/3, K/1, K/2; C = K/3.

references.title: PMK 168/2023
references.locator: arts.12–13, Lampiran A (tarif efektif rata-rata bulanan)
references.quote: For each tax period other than the last, PPh 21 of a permanent employee is the month's gross income (penghasilan bruto: all regular and irregular pay of the month, art.5(1), including the employer-paid JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums; the employer's JHT and JP shares are not income) times the TER rate of the employee's category. Tables as reproduced in the PMK annex, upper bounds inclusive ("s.d."): A (44 brackets, 0% to Rp5,400,000 up to 34% above Rp1,400,000,000), B (40, 0% to Rp6,200,000 up to 34% above Rp1,405,000,000), C (41, 0% to Rp6,600,000 up to 34% above Rp1,419,000,000). The last tax period — December, or the month a permanent employee stops working (art.13) — takes the year's tax at the UU PPh art.17(1)(a) rates on penghasilan kena pajak rounded down to the full thousand: the year's gross less biaya jabatan (5%, at most Rp6,000,000 a year, art.10), less the employee's own JHT and JP contributions, less PTKP; the tax withheld is that tax less the TER already withheld in the year; an excess is returned to the employee in that period (a negative charge). Residents only: CITIZEN and RESIDENT_FOREIGNER; a NON_RESIDENT is taxed under PPh 26.

references.title: PMK 168/2023
references.quote: Art.10(2) and the Lampiran worked examples cap biaya jabatan at Rp500,000 for each month worked in the tax year ("maksimal 4 X Rp500.000,00" for a September joiner). Art.10(1)(b): the employee's own contribution to an OJK-approved pension fund reduces the year's gross like JHT and JP. Art.10(1)(c): zakat or a compulsory religious contribution paid through the employer is deducted. Art.15(3): where the subjective tax obligation starts after January or ends before December (e.g. a foreigner arriving or leaving Indonesia), the net income is annualised (× 12 / months) and the tax prorated (× months / 12); the month the subject status ends is the last tax period. Art.12(2)(b), 16(2)(b) and Lampiran III.1.5(b): a daily worker above Rp2,500,000 a day is taxed at the art.17(1)(a) rates on 50% of each day's gross. Art.1: a pegawai tetap includes one on a fixed-term contract (PKWT) receiving regular income, who has the December/exit reckoning; a monthly-paid PART_TIME or DAILY worker uses monthly TER without a December reckoning. A DAILY worker records pph21_payment_cadence. MONTHLY uses monthly TER. NON_MONTHLY is allowed only for a native one-day DAILY salary run paid that day, with complete ordinary-day attendance, BASIC equal to agreed daily_wage, only BASIC/OVERTIME cash lines, and no unallocated taxable employer premiums. Its actual wage gross, including overtime, determines 0% through Rp450,000, 0.5% through Rp2,500,000, or art.17 on 50% above. Weekly, unit/task, delayed, off-cycle and mixed-payment allocations remain refused. A married female employee takes TK/0 unless she holds a written local-government statement at least at kecamatan level that her husband has no income. Annual PTKP facts come from a real sealed contract covering 1 January, or arrival-month start for a new resident. Without such contract history, exactly one reviewed historical facts.ptkp_standings declaration must cover that exact legal date; source reference, actual review date and complete historical personal/dependency facts are required. A married female employee explicitly declares the husband-income position; a certified no-income declaration requires the written local-government statement reference. No prehire contract, current-value fallback or derived PTKP opening is invented. Owner rule 2026-10-22: PPh 21 is owed on the month's gross, so a payment made before the month's salary run is withheld at what it adds to the month; the TER rate is a flat rate on the month's whole gross and the December/exit reckoning is progressive, so an off-cycle THR or bonus paid first is withheld at the month's bracket, not at the bracket of the bonus alone.

references.title: PMK 168/2023 art.9(4)–(5): PTKP is the declared status at calendar-year start, or arrival part-year start for a new resident. Current marital or dependant changes do not alter that year.
PMK 168/2023
references.quote: The last tax period — December, or the month a permanent employee stops working (art.13) — reckons the year: the year's actual gross less biaya jabatan, the employee's own JHT and JP contributions and PTKP, less the tax already withheld in the tax year. This row reads that year from the payslip history for the tax year — gross_earnings and tax_withheld, the employer's JKK, JKM and BPJS Kesehatan premiums and the employee's JHT and JP, each by scheme — plus this month's ordinary and bonus pay once, so a one-off THR or bonus is counted once in the year it was paid and is never multiplied by the months worked. Months other than the last keep the monthly TER on the month's whole gross (art.12). Two known limits of the stored history: employee_statutory is the run's whole employee contribution (JHT, JP and Kesehatan), so the deduction is 1% of wage wider than art.10(1)(b)'s JHT-and-JP allowance until the payslip stores a per-scheme split; and gross_earnings is the employee's own earnings, so the employer-paid JKK, JKM and Kesehatan premiums (art.5(1)) enter the current month only. The last period's charge is floored at zero because a stored withholding is nonnegative, so an excess is left in the year's withheld tax rather than returned as art.13 requires.
